newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower, Dec/March spread narrows.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower, Dec/March spread narrows.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended lower in choppy, directionless dealings as the Dec/March spread narrowed on weakness in domestic cash premiums, traders said.

"This was a disappointing close technically," a trader said. "We rallied wheat to its highs and sold it right back down. I think the premiums were coming down domestically and people were buying new crop, selling old."
The Dec/March spread, which started at around a 15-1/2 cent per bushel inverse, traded as narrowly as 12-1/2 cents before closing at around 13-1/2 cents, traders said.
KCBT wheat closed 3-1/2 cents per bushel lower to 1/4 cent higher, with Dec down 3-1/2 at $4.38-1/2.
Traders said CIS sold 1.5 million March bushels, Man International bought 1.2 million Dec and LFG sold 1.2 million March. CIS also bull-spread 500,000 Dec/March bushels at 13-1/2 cents.
The KCBT estimated Tuesday's wheat futures volume at 24.545 million bushels, down from 33.495 million Monday.
